literal: Hostility before having-yielded to-behave those-who-are-able-(acc.) who-indeed to-conquer-will-attempt nature they?
translation: Who would even attempt to conquer those who have the strength to yield in the face of hostility?
modern: பகைமை எதிர்ப்படும்போது வளைந்து கொடுத்து நடக்கும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களை வெல்ல நினைக்கும் தன்மையுடையவர் எவரும் இலர்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the strategic value of yielding. When faced with hostility (இகல்), choosing to step back or yield (சாய்ந்து) rather than retaliating is not a weakness, but a profound strength. The poet asks rhetorically who could possibly possess the nature to conquer those who are capable of such disciplined restraint. By yielding, one diffuses the enmity, making it impossible for opponents to achieve a victory over them.
